title: Consent, redaction, retention and deletion: nothing leaves a workspace without its owner's switch, and a deletion leaves nothing behind
request: The owner decided (2026-10-13) that what happens in DCLab may be used to improve it and to train its models, each use off by default, per workspace and per project, customer data included once on, and a table's values never. Retention per class waits on the owner's numbers (proposed 730 days for events and 365 for model text).
spec: Two switches (improve, train) per workspace and per project, changed only by the owner, audited and recorded; redaction of free text before anything leaves; one export that refuses what consent does not allow and never carries cells, prompts, the person or the request; deletion of a project, a draft or a session with everything it left and a tombstone; retention per class, off until set.
plan: dclab_core.redact: rules for e-mails, phones, cards, IBANs, addresses, amounts, ids and names, with counts of what each removed.
dclab_rnd.consent: the switches and the one export (events and decisions).
experience/retention.py: deletion and retention on both stores. Migration 0017 lets only these functions past the append-only triggers, through a transaction-local setting.
Routes for the switches and for deleting a session, the hooks in project and draft deletion, the hourly sweep, and the Admin switches.

decisions.decision: A table's values and model prompts never leave, whatever the consent.
decisions.why: Redaction is a rule, not a guarantee. The only safe way for a value with no shape to leave is not at all.

decisions.decision: The append-only triggers stay, with one door: a transaction-local setting that only the deletion and retention functions set.
decisions.why: An ordinary delete is still refused; the setting ends with its transaction.

decisions.decision: A draft's conversation and decisions follow the consent of the project it became.
decisions.why: A project's goal and its Home history are the same words. Without this, a project with consent off would still leave through its draft.

decisions.decision: Deleting a session removes its events only; its decisions go with their project or draft.
decisions.why: A decision belongs to the work it shaped, not to the visit in which it was made.

change: dclab_core/redact.py (new; dclab-core 0.11.0), dclab_rnd/consent.py (new), dclab_rnd/experience/retention.py (new), dclab_rnd/filelock.py (new), migration 0017, dclab_rnd/agentic/pages/consent.py (new), routers/projects.py, draft/api.py, retention.py, models/usage.py, experience/__init__.py and ledger/__init__.py (the folder lock), audit.py, accounts/guard.py, pages/platform.py, the Admin page; tests/test_consent.py (new), test_experience_log.py, test_accounts.py; .env.example, CLAUDE.md, the plan, the roadmap.

findings.defect: The card-number rule took the spaces around a number.
findings.cause: The repeated group allowed a trailing separator.
findings.fix: The last digit closes the match.

findings.defect: A rewrite of the file record lost events appended while it ran.
findings.scenario: One thread appended 3000 events while another deleted a project in the same visit file: 645 events were lost. Two rewriters shared one temporary file name.
findings.cause: The rewrite did not take the appenders' lock, the lock worked within one process only, and the temporary name was fixed.
findings.fix: filelock.held: a thread lock plus fcntl.flock on the folder, held by every appender and every rewrite. A unique temporary name. A failure is named in the tombstone.

findings.defect: An e-mail address left the workspace through a meta field.
findings.scenario: An upload whose file name held an e-mail address and a person's name was exported verbatim.
findings.cause: Only person and agent text were redacted.
findings.fix: Every string of an exported event is redacted, in lists and dicts too. A file's name leaves as its extension only.

findings.defect: A user id left through a decision label's author.
findings.scenario: A label written by 'person:u3fa9…' was exported with that id.
findings.cause: Labels were exported whole, and answers kept their source (possibly a request id).
findings.fix: Who labelled leaves by kind only. An answer's source stays home.

findings.defect: A project's train switch could not be turned off once the earlier opt-in was on.
findings.scenario: With share_for_training set, setting consent.train to false changed nothing.
findings.cause: Train was computed as the OR of the two.
findings.fix: The project's own switch, once set, wins, and setting either writes both.

findings.defect: A project with consent off still had its Home conversation exported.
findings.scenario: The draft's draft.created was exported under the workspace's consent.
findings.cause: Events without a project followed the workspace only.
findings.fix: A draft's events and decisions follow the project it was built into.

findings.defect: Redaction missed names at the start of a sentence, names next to the product's words, and short ids.
findings.scenario: 'Jane Roe asked', 'ask the Owner Jane Roe', 'Mohammad Reza Hosseini' and 'ORD12345' all passed.
findings.cause: Names were skipped at sentence starts, a known word anywhere in a match exempted all of it, and ids needed a hyphen or six digits.
findings.fix: Known words are trimmed from the ends of a match and the rest is redacted. An id is any mixed run of letters and digits with at least three digits.

findings.scenario: Dates became phone numbers, '5-fold' and 'WF-01' became ids, 'rows 1000 2000 3000 4000' became a card.
findings.cause: The phone, id and card rules were too wide.
findings.fix: A phone has a phone's shape. Dates, '-fold' and the product's codes pass. A card must pass the Luhn check and must not be mostly zeros.

findings.defect: Prompts kept in the gateway's usage log escaped both retention and deletion.
findings.scenario: With prompts logged, deleting a project left its prompts in model_request.
findings.cause: Only the session record was swept.
findings.fix: forget_prompts on both usage stores, called by the sweep (by age) and by project and draft deletion. Spend rows stay.

findings.defect: Deleting a session was claimed to remove its decisions, and several faults had no test.
findings.scenario: Owner-only routes were never called by another role; ids, drafts and lists were untested.
findings.cause: The suite runs without accounts, and the test events carried no user or request.
findings.fix: The claim was corrected. test_accounts calls every timelines route with the wrong role. Tests were added for each case.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each fix undone fails a test
measurements.result: 13 of 15 caught at first; one guard found redundant and removed, one test added; then all caught

measurements.name: lost events under a concurrent deletion
measurements.result: 645 of 3000 lost before the lock, 0 of 400 after
limits: One machine, threads in one process; the flock covers other processes by design, not by this test.

outcome: Consent is two switches per workspace and per project, off until the owner turns them on. The export obeys them and never carries cells, prompts, the person or the request. A deletion removes everything the project, draft or session left and leaves a tombstone; retention per class waits on the owner's numbers.
lessons: Every field that leaves is a path for a person's data, whatever its class: redact them all, not only the fields marked as text.
A file store that is append-only by convention needs one lock that every writer holds before anything may rewrite it.
Two switches with one meaning must move together, or one of them cannot be turned off.
risks: Redaction is a rule: a lower-case name or a value with no shape passes. That is why cells and prompts never leave.
An export already made is not recalled by a later deletion: there is no tombstone inside a dataset yet (19.12, 19.13).
